title: Learning Energy-Based Models from Stochastic Interpolants using Spatiotemporal Differences
claim: Methods using only one kind of difference fail under specific data conditions, while the joint approach avoids both failure modes.
layout: 4 panels left-to-right, one density sketch then three error heatmaps sharing a colorbar
description: Four panels in a row. Panel (a) shows a blue gradient interpolant density over x (vertical axis) and t (horizontal axis, 0 to 1). Overlaid arrows mark the three ways to learn it: a vertical black arrow labeled Spatial, a horizontal black arrow labeled Temporal, and a diagonal magenta arrow labeled Spatiotemporal. Panels (b), (c) and (d) are white-to-dark-red heatmaps of estimation error. The x-axis is multimodality and the y-axis is support mismatch, both from 0 to 1. Temporal (b) has high error along the top, with a red upward arrow and the text 'Error increases'. Spatial (c) has high error at the right, with a red rightward arrow and 'Error increases'. Spatiotemporal (d) is almost entirely white, labeled 'No error'. A shared error colorbar sits on the far right. The eye goes first to the red regions and then to the blank panel (d).
caption: (a): interpolant density pd(x, t). We learn it via spatial differences which vary x but fix t, temporal differences which vary t but fix x, or spatiotemporal differences that vary both x and t. (b), (c), (d): empirical error of different learning methods when trained to model the stochastic interpolant between standard normal noise and data given by a one-dimensional Gaussian mixture with two components, where the means vary and the standard deviation is fixed. Temporal methods incur high estimation error when the data distribution has high density in low density region of the noise distribution (the means of data components are far from high density region of standard noral noise, abusively, “support mismatch”). Spatial methods incur high estimation error when the data distribution is multi-modal (the two components are far apart). Our spatiotemporal method achieves here virtually zero error in both setups. Further details are provided in Section 6.1 and Appendix E.4.
abstract: Learning an energy-based model from data samples is a central problem in machine learning. Many recent and popular methods, such as denoising score matching for training energy-based diffusion models, use stochastic interpolants to corrupt data samples at different noise levels indexed by a time variable. This defines a joint density over both the data space and time, and most methods learn its energy through either spatial or temporal differences. We identify distinct failure modes for both of these approaches. To solve them, we propose Spatiotemporal Noise-Contrastive Estimation (stNCE), a framework for learning the energy through joint spatiotemporal differences. stNCE unifies many existing methods and leads to new training objectives. Experiments on images and molecules demonstrate performance competitive with state-of-the-art density estimation methods.
